choice: Compete with human play, initially Mohammad
explanation: Train a game-playing model and compare its performance with the user. A numerical competitive threshold is separate.
reason: User wants to see how far the model can go and cites PPO in Dota as motivation. No success or duration guarantee.
next: Agree on competitive threshold and matched comparison conditions.

choice: Explain and obtain user approval for each design choice
explanation: Proposals remain proposals until the user understands and approves them. Approval of a setting does not authorize a long run.
reason: User wants understanding and control this time.
next: Continue recording approval, reason, limits and superseding changes.

choice: Fresh model; exact reset contract still open
explanation: No reuse of old learned policy is intended. Fresh optimizer and no imitation initialization are proposed details, not separately confirmed.
reason: User explicitly requested a fresh model with refined rules.
next: Confirm optimizer reset, initialization and allowed code reuse.

choice: Maskable PPO is the selected project direction
explanation: The user named the new branch and project Maskable PPO. The existing legacy trainer already uses it, but its configuration is not adopted.
reason: User-selected direction. No separate algorithm comparison was approved. Dota is motivation, not game-specific evidence.
next: Review a concrete architecture and PPO configuration.

choice: Accepted simulator from main, f34 identified
explanation: User accepts accuracy for this project. Inspected remote main source is 938b9f8 / 2026-11-10.f34. This is not a new parity certification.
reason: User says the simulator is now accurate to their liking.
next: Use the accepted source and verify a matching build before any run.

choice: Maskable-PPO ref found; experiment workspace not prepared
explanation: Remote Maskable-PPO and main were verified at 938b9f8. Current checkout is still dirty codex/driveway-physics; no switch or transfer was made.
reason: Engineering requirement: keep the experiment and evidence tied to the intended source rather than this older checkout.
next: Prepare the intended workspace and transfer approved records without losing existing edits.

choice: Road, bridge, roundabout, motorway, delete, weekly choice, wait
explanation: These are the user-listed actions. Additional tools or driveway/motorway-edit controls are not silently added.
reason: Explicit user scope; no additional rationale was supplied.
next: Specify each remaining tool and any required editing controls.

choice: Strictly no externally generated routes
explanation: No route candidates, suggested paths or automatic endpoint-to-endpoint road completion. The model determines construction geometry. Ordinary vehicle routing is unaffected.
reason: User explicitly made this a strict rule. No separate rationale was supplied.
next: Ensure the implementation and masks never choose routes for the model.

choice: Only physically impossible moves are excluded
explanation: Physical game rules, stock and current state determine legality. Legal but unproductive or strategically poor edits stay available.
reason: Explicit user criterion. Discussion emphasized retaining geometric freedom.
next: Audit mask versus host agreement for each tool and selection stage.

choice: One neighboring connection per completed action
explanation: Model selects two adjacent grid positions. Each edit changes the network and returns an observation while paused. Long routes are composed by the model.
reason: Reviewed benefit: fine control over bends, branches, shared roads and repairs. More decisions before score feedback is an accepted risk.
next: Choose neural output encoding and staged-selection behavior.

choice: Include legal diagonals as well as horizontal/vertical
explanation: All eight neighboring directions are in scope wherever simulator rules permit. The B-D example illustrated a diagonal, not arbitrary-distance linking.
reason: User corrected the example to include B-D. Existing legal connections must not be omitted.
next: Enforce actual terrain, crossing, parcel and driveway rules.

choice: Incremental neighboring connections across water
explanation: Model chooses successive connections across water, with no automatic full crossing. Accepted f34 source permits incomplete spans and extensions.
reason: User reason: a bridge is a road on water.
next: Implement water legality and span material accounting; tool encoding remains open.

choice: No placement contract selected
explanation: Need to define the selected center, footprint and interaction with existing roads under accepted simulator rules.
reason: Not chosen. A precise contract is needed for inputs, legality and execution.
next: Inspect accepted rules and present center-placement semantics for approval.

choice: Endpoint and editing contract not selected
explanation: Need to define endpoint selection, orientation if required, slots, editing and removal. No land-road path generation is permitted.
reason: Not chosen. Motorway control differs from neighboring road construction.
next: Explain and approve endpoint and lifecycle controls.

choice: Removal target granularity not selected
explanation: Need to choose connection, tile or structure targets and expose pending clearance/refunds correctly.
reason: Not chosen. Different removal targets permit different repairs and affect stock.
next: Review removal behavior for each approved infrastructure type.

choice: Choose among offered packages; exact encoding open
explanation: User included weekly item selection. Paused selection and early return from wait are approved; package-index/action encoding is not.
reason: User scope. Engineering reason for early return: return control when input is required.
next: Define offered-package observations and selectable actions.

choice: Multiple sequential edits without advancing game time
explanation: Build/delete actions return updated observations. The model can choose another edit or wait. It need not emit an entire plan at once.
reason: User pauses for construction and leaves simple work running. Equal permission to pause is the comparison premise.
next: Implement explicit clock semantics and test update-without-time behavior.

choice: One simulated second; early stop for game-over/weekly choice
explanation: Fixed initial wait length. Weekly selection is paused. Other event interruptions or longer wait choices are not approved.
reason: Reviewed rationale: simple reproducible pacing and frequent chances to intervene, accepting quiet-period overhead initially. Not measured optimal.
next: Implement and verify duration and early-return semantics.

choice: No cap or operational stall rule chosen
explanation: Repeated edits can avoid advancing time indefinitely. No extra mask, penalty or edit-count limit has been approved.
reason: Not chosen. A practical run must distinguish a stalled policy from normal paused construction without inventing game illegality.
next: Explain candidate operational handling and seek approval.

choice: Tool/position/direction prediction layout not selected
explanation: One completed edit does not necessarily equal one neural prediction. Joint or staged selections need compatible masks and recorded selection state.
reason: Not chosen. Must express approved control without unmanageable or inconsistent choices.
next: Compare a concrete joint/staged interface after all tool semantics are defined.

choice: No explicit house/destination goal selection adopted
explanation: Model may choose local edits directly. An explicit persistent goal layer would be an additional design, not required by neighboring edges.
reason: Discussion distinguished strategic goal selection from local edit parameters. No hierarchy was selected.
next: Decide whether the initial policy acts directly or has explicit goals; no generated routes either way.

choice: Structured visible game state approved
explanation: Geography, revealed bounds, buildings/colors/entrances, infrastructure/connections, visible demand, traffic/recent movement, stock/offers, time and selection state.
reason: Engineering rationale reviewed and approved: provide visible geometry/status directly without an image-recognition prerequisite. No separate user rationale supplied.
next: Translate approved groups into exact fields and audit visibility.

choice: Exclude future/RNG and engineered route answers
explanation: Approved observation proposal excludes hidden spawn schedules, RNG state and best-route labels. Exact timer/reservation fields require visibility review.
reason: Reviewed rationale: use player-accessible state and keep route construction with the model. Structured perception still differs from human vision.
next: Audit each proposed field against accepted visible game information.

choice: Exact grid/vector channels and scaling open
explanation: Need channel definitions, dimensions, color encoding, normalization, selection state and any optional score input.
reason: Not chosen. Consistent inputs must represent the approved contents without losing connections or leaking hidden state.
next: Present an explicit input schema for approval.

choice: Recent movement approved; sampling and length open
explanation: Need recent observations or movement summaries tied to simulated timestamps. Paused edits must not create fake movement history.
reason: Reviewed reason: a single image of cars cannot reliably distinguish movement from a queue.
next: Choose history length, sampling interval and representation.

choice: Game score only is the chosen direction
explanation: No connection, survival or construction bonuses are adopted. Exact reward calculation and discount remain separate decisions.
reason: User preference: only the game score. No additional reason was supplied.
next: Approve the concrete reward implementation and verify simulator score semantics.

choice: Proposed score-after minus score-before
explanation: Score increases would be delivered per transition. The undiscounted sum equals episode score change. This formula is not yet separately approved.
reason: Engineering proposal: reward the actual score while avoiding invented shaping bonuses or penalties.
next: Approve formula and terminal/cap behavior.

choice: Discount, GAE and zero-time edit treatment open
explanation: Standard per-decision discount counts paused edits as well as waits. Longer edit sequences can put completed trips farther from earlier decisions.
reason: Not chosen. Timing and credit assignment must be designed together, without silently changing score-only reward.
next: Explain candidate discount/GAE settings and any nonstandard timing work.

choice: All but one city train; different seeds validate; unseen city tests
explanation: Direction supplied by user. Exact held-out city, seed counts/lists, learner seeds and city sampling are not selected.
reason: User proposed this split; engineering rationale is separating development from final unseen-city evidence.
next: Approve held-out city, train/validation/test seed lists and balancing.

choice: No curriculum or seed-repeat schedule chosen
explanation: Whether to begin on easier states, all training cities or repeated seeds remains unresolved. Historical defaults are not adopted.
reason: Not chosen. Sampling changes what experience the learner receives and what generalization is tested.
next: Choose initial sampling and any progression criteria.

choice: Same simulator and pause permission; full protocol open
explanation: Need matched city/seed exposure, tools, timing/caps, attempts and competitive threshold. User permits pauses but sometimes edits simple things while running.
reason: User goal is competition with himself; engineering proposal is a controlled comparison.
next: Agree conditions and record human scores under them.

choice: Metrics, cohort sizes and baselines not selected
explanation: Candidate evidence includes score distributions, survival/cap status, failure reasons, learner seeds and sampled/deterministic behavior. Generated-route baselines are prohibited here.
reason: Not chosen. A best game alone cannot establish reliable competitive performance.
next: Approve numeric protocol and permissible untrained/random/manual baselines.

choice: Validation cadence and promotion rule open
explanation: Need when to evaluate, how to select a checkpoint and when to stop or roll back. Final test outcomes must not guide ongoing tuning.
reason: Not chosen. Fix selection criteria before seeing results to reduce selection bias.
next: Approve validation/checkpoint selection and final-test usage rules.

choice: User can review best, worst and average-scoring games
explanation: Preserve replays and scores for the user, not just a best-game highlight.
reason: User explicitly requested personal evaluation of all three performance levels.
next: Approve precise replay cohort and selection details.

choice: Frozen checkpoint and nearest-mean episode proposed
explanation: Proposal: evaluate one fixed checkpoint, choose highest/lowest and the real episode nearest cohort arithmetic mean; label checkpoint/cohort/ties.
reason: Engineering rationale: games should describe the same policy and average should be an actual replay.
next: Approve cohort, timing, tie handling and selection method.

choice: Structure and size not selected
explanation: A compact spatial network plus global inputs was proposed. No layer sizes or memory architecture adopted.
reason: Not chosen. Network must match finalized input/output semantics and hardware workload.
next: Present architecture, capacity and parameter count after schema decisions.

choice: Numeric settings not selected
explanation: Learning rate, rollout length, batch size, epochs, clipping, entropy, value loss and gradient limits remain open. Discount/GAE tracked separately.
reason: Not chosen. Old trainer defaults and library defaults are not evidence of suitability.
next: Explain each numeric starting setting and approve one initial configuration.

choice: Runtime versions and CPU/GPU mode open
explanation: No new environment pins, GPU stack or exact reproducibility contract adopted. Existing requirements are historical context.
reason: Not chosen. Need a reproducible executable setup on the intended machines.
next: Verify compatible versions and approve environment/device choices.

choice: Current laptop and tentative Alienware desktop
explanation: Laptop verified: i7-1185G7 4C/8T,31.7GiB,Intel Iris Xe,476.9GiB SSD. Desktop reported: i7-10700KF,2080 Super 8GB,16GB RAM. Desktop unverified.
reason: User names these machines as available. Inventory is not a throughput benchmark.
next: Verify desktop identification and benchmark the chosen workload.

choice: Machine roles, workers and distribution open
explanation: Desktop-primary/laptop-development is a hypothesis. No speedup, worker count or distributed learner selected.
reason: Not chosen. Simulator and learner costs may bottleneck differently.
next: Benchmark before choosing machine roles and parallelism.

choice: Game-time cap and truncation semantics open
explanation: Game-over ends the episode; external caps, interrupted runs and time limits need explicit handling separate from failure.
reason: Not chosen. Artificial limits affect evaluation and value bootstrapping.
next: Approve caps and termination/truncation handling.

choice: No run budget or launch authorization yet
explanation: Need bounded pilot duration/steps, integration checks, save/reload/evaluation checks, logs and pass/stop criteria before any long run.
reason: User requires understanding and approval. Earlier design approval does not authorize training.
next: Finish specification, present checks and finite budget, then obtain run approval.

choice: Chronological durable records with archived small sources
explanation: Maintain experiment history, simulator decisions, current status and evidence archives. Keep weights/binaries/private source/secrets out of commits.
reason: User explicitly requires every material choice/finding and its reason to remain documented.
next: Keep records current; archive each future report without overwriting history.
